column1: # Scripted property-function wiring and expectation, for every case whose manifest
# `source` is `relation` — and for no other case.
# Columns: case <TAB> emits <TAB> stop-handling <TAB> cancel-on-pull <TAB> invocations <TAB> pulls
#   emits          rows the relation emits per invocation, which is also the bound it
#                  DECLARES (`PropertyFunction::rows_per_invocation`). The declaration is
#                  held to an upper-bound honesty contract; the corpus keeps it exact so a
#                  change to what a relation declares shows up as a change in spend.
#   stop-handling  honours  the cursor polls the caller's signal and abandons the
#                           invocation on a fired one — what a relation CAN do
#                  ignores  the cursor never reads the signal at all — what a relation
#                           that cannot abandon an invocation it is inside does
#   cancel-on-pull never    the relation has no effect on the caller's signal
#                  <n>      the relation cancels the caller's flag at the start of its
#                           n-th pull (1-based), standing in for a host that cancels while
#                           the evaluator is inside a relation and can poll nothing
#   invocations    the exact number of times the relation was opened
#   pulls          the exact number of rows the relation was asked to produce
# `invocations` and `pulls` are DERIVED by the corpus regeneration step and re-checked on
# every run. They are the observations that separate "the ceiling prevented the work" from
# "the work was done and its rows discarded", which no governor evidence can distinguish.
